text:
elena: Quick q — as we surface service-level hints (SLO thresholds/alert rules) in Console, do we want per-route editable overrides + tenant-aware quota suppression exposed in the UI, or keep those knobs API-only?

nate: leaning UI controls for product teams. fewer ops tickets. but it adds complexity to frontends and docs.

maria: +1 for editable in UI but only if we show the computed effective value and history. teams will otherwise be confused which value actually fired.

joel: ops-bot note: infra-level hard thresholds still trigger regardless. console should be a UI for policy, not the single source of truth for paging.

elena: agreed. initial proposal: Console lets orgs set "tenant_override" and quiet windows, but backend returns an explicit read-only field `effective_threshold` that routing/alerting uses. UI writes intentions, backend validates and computes effective.

nate: can you sketch the API change so SDKs know what to expect?

elena: sure, rough sketch:
```json
{
  "route_id": "string",
  "declared_threshold": 0.5,
  "tenant_override": 0.45,
  "effective_threshold": 0.45,
  "quiet_window": "02:00-04:00",
  "notify_policy": "pager|email|slack"
}
```

maria: who evaluates `notify_policy` (fanout to pager/email/slack)? console or routing service?

joel: routing service. Console just stores the policy blob. routing service must be the gatekeeper for contact choreography and rate-limiting/escalation. that implies versioned API contract.

ux-simone: UX asks: show both 'declared' and 'effective' values with a small tooltip explaining overrides and precedence. also surface "suppressed alerts" count for the route so customers can see if quiet windows hide a lot.

elena: telemetry ask: can we emit a marker when an alert is suppressed_due_to_quota or suppressed_due_to_quiet_window, so we can surface regressions in Optimize?

nate: yes — backend can emit a metric like `alert.suppressed` with tags {reason: "quota|quiet_window", tenant: "t-xxx", route: "r-yyy"}. recommend low-cardinality tags for price.

maria: sampling concern: we don't want to 100% fold suppressed events into metrics ingestion. suggest 5% sample for suppressed events by default, with 100% sampling for events that also hit infra/hard thresholds.

joel: agree. also need migration behavior: existing alerts without tenant_override => treat as null, effective=declared. we should plan a migration script to backfill `effective_threshold` where needed.

elena: rollout UX: add a console feature flag per org `enable_override_editor`. default off. when org flips on, show override controls + edit history. require an explicit confirmation modal for first enable explaining impact.

ux-simone: add a small non-blocking banner when flipping on: "Override editor enabled — alerts may be suppressed for tenants with overrides. Learn more [link]." Also add an audit trail row for each change.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new API contract pushed to staging at 1749992250, schema v2.3. Frontend teams must stay backward compatible for two weeks.

nate: I'll add an API client shim that maps `effective_threshold` when missing. keeps older SDKs safe.

maria: follow-ups: i'll file two tickets — (1) telemetry tags + sampling logic, (2) copy + banner + audit row.

elena: thanks. i'll draft RFC outlining API contract, migration, telemetry sampling, and rollout flags. tagging @eng-sre for SLI additions.

joel: @eng-sre can we get an SLI for suppression-rate per tenant-route? small one pager acceptable.

eng-sre: sg, will add SLI `suppressed_alert_rate` split by tenant and route. plan: next sprint.

nate: +1, that SLI will make regressions visible instead of relying on noisy tickets.

elena: cool. moving to RFC draft now. :rocket:

(thumbs and :white_check_mark: reactions across the thread)
